questions.text: Consider a disk queue with requests for I/O to blocks on cylinders 47,38,121,191,87,11, 92, 10. The C-LOOK scheduling algorithm is used. The head is initially at cylinder number 63, moving to wards larger cylinder numbers on its servicing pass. The cylinders are numbered from 0to 199. The total head movement (in number of cylinders) incurred while servicing these requests is____ .
questions.solution:
C-LOOK from 63 going up: 87, 92, 121, 191 (movement 191 [latex]-[/latex] 63 = 128), then jump to the lowest request 10 (191 [latex]-[/latex] 10 = 181), then 11, 38, 47 (47 [latex]-[/latex] 10 = 37).

Total = 128 + 181 + 37 = 346

Answer: 346

questions.text:
Consider a computer system with 40-bit virtual addressing and page size of sixteen
kilobytes. If the computer system has a one level page table per process and each page table entry requires 48 bits, then the size of the per-process page table is _________ mega bytes.
questions.solution:
Entries = [latex]\frac{2^{40}}{2^{14}}=2^{26}[/latex]. Each entry = 48 bits = 6 bytes.

Size [latex]=2^{26}\times6=6\times64\text{ MB}=384[/latex] MB

Answer: 384

questions.text:
Consider an arbitrary set of CPU-bound processes with unequal CPU burst lengths
submitted at the same time to a computer system.Which one of the following process scheduling algorithms would minimize the average waiting time in the ready queue?
questions.solution:
All processes arrive together, so shortest remaining time first behaves like SJF, which is optimal for average waiting time. Round robin, random order or "long jobs first" make short jobs wait longer.

Answer: Shortest remaining time first

questions.text: A processor can support a maximum memory of 4GB, where the memory is word-addressable (a word consists of two bytes). The size of the address bus of the process or is at least bits________.
questions.solution:
4 GB = [latex]2^{32}[/latex] bytes. One word = 2 bytes, so there are [latex]2^{31}[/latex] words.
Word addressable [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]2^{31}[/latex] addresses [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 31 address bits.

Answer: 31

questions.text: Dirty bit for a page in a page table
questions.solution:
A page is written back to disk on replacement only if its dirty bit is set (it was modified). Clean pages are simply discarded, avoiding unnecessary writes.

Answer: helps avoid unnecessary writes on a paging device
